correctness.rationale: For the ordinary graph Morse complex, exhaustively checked equivalence between gradient arrow systems and directed forests yields 1791 simplices with dimension-count vector (18,126,432,729,486). The augmented mod-2 ranks (1,17,109,323,406) saturate successive Q-rank upper bounds from boundary composition zero, so only reduced rational H_4 remains (dimension 80). Signed simplex traces for all 72 graph automorphisms agree with a second orbit-cycle-parity method on every fixed face. Reduced Lefschetz, subtracting the H_0 character, gives the complete nine-class character; its inner products with nine orthonormal rational irreducible characters give multiplicities (1,2,1,2,4,5,3,4,4), all nonnegative. Their weighted dimensions total 80, and the squared irreducible dimensions sum to 72. The extracted standalone verifier prints VERIFY_OK. Finite complete enumeration here proves a finite statement, not a general theorem for all bipartite graphs.

originality.rationale: The exact prior nonequivariant 80-sphere calculation is not claimed as new. The earliest automorphism-group paper identifies Aut(M(K3,3)) as S3 wr C2 but does not give its action on homology. The connectivity and star-cluster papers neither state nor imply the full nine-class character. Exact and semantic searches for equivariant homology, bipartition swap, rational irreducible decomposition, and rooted-forest formulations found no direct covering record. Their failure is not proof of universal novelty; unindexed or inaccessible sources remain a genuine risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent equivariant calculation might be unindexed, cited only under an alternate rooted-forest terminology, or inaccessible.

value.rationale: K3,3 is the smallest balanced genuinely two-sided complete bipartite graph whose Morse complex has a large nontrivial top homology. Determining its complete S3 wr C2 module answers a natural equivariant refinement of the topology and automorphism-group problems studied by arXiv:1904.10907 and arXiv:2004.10481. The novel symmetry-fixed dimension one and bipartition-swap eigenspaces 38 and 42 are not implied by dimension 80 and can guide equivariant comparisons. The result is a complete canonical representation, not an arbitrary parameter slice or an isolated unsupported statistic.
